questions.question:

Authenticate
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Discredit**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Authenticate"** means to prove or show something to be true, valid, or genuine. (सत्यापित करना)

 
 
• **Example:** The bank authenticated her identity by verifying her documents.
 
 
 
• **"Discredit"** means to harm the reputation of someone or something, or to show that something is false or unreliable. (अपयश देना, अविश्वसनीय बनाना)
 
 
• **Example:** The report discredited the politician by exposing their fraudulent activities.
 
 
 
• Hence, the antonym of **'Authenticate'** is **'Discredit'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Discredit**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Entitle **(अधिकार देना): To give someone a legal right or a claim to something.

 
 
• **Example:** Everyone is entitled to a fair trial under the law.
 
 
 
• **Scatter **(बिखेरना): To throw or distribute things in different directions.
 
 
• **Example:** The wind scattered the leaves across the garden.
 
 
 
• **Amalgamate **(मिलाना): To combine or unite to form one organization or structure.
 
 
• **Example:** The two companies decided to amalgamate to increase their market share.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank.

Neither John _____ his friends were able to attend the party.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. nor .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence uses the construction **"Neither...nor," **which is a **correlative conjunction** used to connect two negative ideas.
 
• In this case, the sentence requires** "nor"** to complete the structure and make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• The correct pair is: **"Neither...nor."**

Correct sentence: *Neither John **nor** his friends were able to attend the party.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Correlative Conjunctions:**

 
 
• Correlative conjunctions are pairs of words that work together to link related elements in a sentence.
 
• Examples include: **neither...nor, either...or, both...and, not only...but also**.
 
 
 
• **Usage of Neither...Nor:**
 
 
• **Neither...nor** is used to join two negative ideas.
 
• **Example:** Neither the teacher nor the students were present.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Learning a new language can be __all challenging and rewarding.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. both challenging and rewarding.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined phrase "all challenging and rewarding" is grammatically incorrect and does not convey the intended meaning properly.
 
• The correct substitution is **"both challenging and rewarding," **which clearly expresses that learning a new language is both of these qualities simultaneously.
 
• Using **"both"** emphasizes that the action or experience is equally challenging and rewarding.

Correct sentence: *Learning a new language can be **both challenging and rewarding**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common usage of "both":**

 
 
• "Both" is used to link two qualities or elements that coexist or are equally applicable.
 
 
• Example: She is both intelligent and kind.
 
• Usage: It emphasizes dual characteristics or actions.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Incorrect alternatives:**
 
 
• "Whether both challenging and rewarding" is awkward and does not fit the sentence structure.
 
• "All both challenging or rewarding" is redundant and grammatically incorrect.
 
• "Neither challenging and rewarding" changes the meaning of the sentence entirely.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Elastocaloric cooling is a promising, eco-friendly technology for refrigeration that has the __potential to be used by__ a broad range of applications and at different temperature ranges.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. potential to be used in .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"potential to be used by"** is inappropriate in the context of the sentence because applications do not "use" the technology themselves; rather, it is used** "in"** applications.
 
• The correct preposition in this context is **"in,"** since it specifies that the technology can be applied or utilized within a broad range of applications.
 
• The revised phrase **"potential to be used in" **correctly conveys that elastocaloric cooling can be employed within various applications.

Correct sentence: *Elastocaloric cooling is a promising, eco-friendly technology for refrigeration that has the **potential to be used in** a broad range of applications and at different temperature ranges.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prepositions:**

 
 
• Prepositions such as "in," "on," and "by" are used to clarify relationships between words in a sentence.
 
• For example, "used in" indicates the context or area of application, while "used by" indicates the agent or user.
 
 
 
• **Contextual Usage:**
 
 
• Understanding context is essential for choosing the correct preposition, as it affects the clarity and accuracy of the sentence.
